title: The month after a SNAP transition, resources still move more than jobs or hours
source_unit: identified SIPP person, SNAP transition at month t to t+1, followed by resource/earnings/hours/job change at t+1 to t+2

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP no -> yes; household resource ratio

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric THINCPOV in the transition-following months

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive following context; SNAP state changes at t→t+1 and THINCPOV changes at t+1→t+2; WPFINWGT from t and replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Selected transition triples; this is not a post-treatment causal estimate or benefit-adequacy measure.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with valid following household resource-ratio context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Resource decline may reflect timing, household composition, reporting, or an unmeasured shock rather than SNAP effect.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP no -> yes; person earnings

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric TPEARN in the following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method using monthly person earnings TPEARN.
observations.uncertainty: Small selected person-earnings universe; not household earnings, hourly pay, or causal recovery.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering SNAP with valid person-earnings context in the following month.
observations.counterinterpretation: Earnings increases and declines can reflect timing, job composition, days worked, reporting, or other changes.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP no -> yes; person hours

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric TMWKHRS in the following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method using monthly average hours TMWKHRS.
observations.uncertainty: Job-holder-conditioned and selected; stable hours do not establish stable pay, quality, or control.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering SNAP with valid following person-hours context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Hours may be stable while earnings, schedule control, or household security change.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP no -> yes; job count

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric RMNUMJOBS in the following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method using monthly RMNUMJOBS.
observations.uncertainty: Selected valid job-count universe; no work-quality, pay, or causal claim.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering SNAP with valid following job-count context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable job count can coexist with changing hours, earnings, quality, or household resources.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP yes -> no; household resource ratio

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric THINCPOV in the transition-following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method for SNAP exit.
observations.uncertainty: Selected transition triples; exit does not identify restored security or program effect.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt with valid following household resource-ratio context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Decline can reflect renewal, reporting, timing, household, earnings, or other shocks.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP yes -> no; person earnings

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric TPEARN in the following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method using monthly person earnings TPEARN.
observations.uncertainty: Small selected person-earnings universe; earnings increases do not establish exit-to-work or restored security.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting SNAP with valid following person-earnings context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Earnings recovery may reflect work timing, composition, reporting, or other income changes.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP yes -> no; person hours

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric TMWKHRS in the following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method using monthly average hours TMWKHRS.
observations.uncertainty: Job-holder-conditioned and selected; stable hours do not establish restored pay or security.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting SNAP with valid following person-hours context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable hours may coexist with changing pay, job quality, household resources, or program administration.

observations.period: 2024; after SNAP yes -> no; job count

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric RMNUMJOBS in the following months

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR method using monthly RMNUMJOBS.
observations.uncertainty: Selected valid job-count universe; no work-quality, pay, or causal claim.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting SNAP with valid following job-count context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable job count does not establish stable household resources, earnings, hours, or security.

related_sources.claim: The audit preserves the three-month input, replicate archive, matched following pairs, hashes, and Fay-BRR method.

boundary: This record follows selected person-level SNAP transitions one month forward. It does not estimate SNAP effects, benefit adequacy, notice, effort, remedy, care, trust, political action, or restored security. Outcome universes differ: THINCPOV is household-level, TPEARN and TMWKHRS person/job-holder-level, and RMNUMJOBS person-level.
